claims.statement: If every required closure predicate is true for the same bound subject, the model selects halt/closed.
An open obligation prevents proof closure.
A subject mutation prevents inheritance of the predecessor's proof closure.
Repeated verification after closure is not new proof progress for the unchanged subject.
Proof closure is relative to an explicit subject, obligation set, evidence set, verifier set and time.
claims.scope: Does not establish external truth beyond those bindings.

claims.statement: The closure rule can be expressed as an application-layer terminality condition for evidence-bound effect protocols.
claims.scope: Individual Internet-Draft candidate; no IETF consensus claimed.
